newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to approve amendments to E-VAT tax.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to approve amendments to E-VAT tax.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos will sign into law a bill making amendments to the expanded value added tax (E-VAT), a Palace statement said on Tuesday.
The bill to be signed on Wednesday will amend some provisions of E-VAT which was passed early this year.

E-VAT was introduced as part of the country's reform measures aimed at simplifying the tax system to improve compliance and collections. The new tax had replaced more than 80 indirect taxes on a wide range of goods and services.
But there were complaints that some sectors were unfairly taxed while others were exempt from the burden.
"The President had described the contested provisions of the E-VAT law as 'undoubtedly burdensome to our people'" the Palace statement said.
The Philippine National News agency said the amendments will exempt from E-VAT the following items:

Sale of non-food agricultural products, marine and forest products, cotton and cotton seed, copra, fertilisers, seeds, fish, prawn, livestock and poultry feeds, coal and natural gas, petroleum products except lubricating oil, processed gas, grease and wax.
The Palace did not mention the exemptions but listed sectors which would come under the tax umbrella after the amendments.

Those who will be taxed include stock brokers, real estate agents, construction and service contractors and customs and immigration brokers, it said. Hotel and restaurant operators and taxi services would also be taxed, it said.

Two other bills that President Ramos will sign on Wenesday are the Armed Forces of the Philippines modernisation programme and a measure increasing the number of divisions and Justices of the Court of Appeals, the Palace said.
